chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) used to say:

"When two 'Eids (festivals) gather for the people on one day, it is appropriate for the Imam to say to the people in his first sermon: 'Two 'Eids have gathered for you, so I will pray both of them together. Whoever is distant and wishes to depart from the second, I have given him permission.'

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya said: 'I took this hadith from the book of Muhammad ibn Hamzah ibn al-Yasa', who narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, and I did not hear it directly from him.' (305) 37 And - from him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both) who said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade weapons from being taken out on the two 'Eids, unless there is a visible enemy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two Eid festivals fall on the same day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of combining the two Eid prayers under the leadership of the Imam, emphasizing communal unity while providing practical leniency for those with distance or specific needs to depart after the first prayer. The accompanying report prohibiting the display of weapons unless facing a visible enemy highlights the festive, peaceful nature of Eid, distinguishing it from times of war or political tension, a point of significant jurisprudential discussion among Shia scholars regarding the conditions of 'visibility' of the enemy.
